title: The firewall that allowed on error
blurb: An internal error returned allow, and the detector failure skipped the backstop.
prompt: During a detector outage, injection attempts passed because the draft mapped every exception to allow and skipped the lexical backstop once the model call had failed. The same draft logged matched span text. Review it, fix it, and prove failures block and logs carry no prompt content.
aiNote: The draft catches every internal error and returns allow, so an outage opens the firewall completely, and when the detector fails it skips the lexical backstop instead of falling through to it.
testIdea: Stub the detector to fail and assert a known injection pattern is still blocked or stripped by the backstop; trigger an internal error and assert block with no prompt in the body; inspect an event payload for span text.
followUps: Which patterns deserve block versus strip?
How do you tune rules without storing the prompts that matched?
What makes an injection rule durable against paraphrase?
